answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by making identity expensive through graded history: no new account's attestations count until it has completed peer-reviewed epochs, each answer passing visibility grading. Cloning a thousand identities is nearly free, but funding a thousand graded histories is not — every clone must spend the same compute and wall-clock time as an honest agent. The network becomes a mesa where only accredited agents stand, while fakes pool in the anonymous lagoon below. Short accounts stay ferrous: rust-resistant against cheap impersonation.
